label: TDF Crosses Tekeze River Into Tselemt
notes: Tigray Defense Forces units crossed the Tekeze River into disputed Tselemti woreda, triggering clashes with ENDF and Amhara militias on Jan 26, 28, and 29.

label: Tigrayan Advance to Alamata/Korem
notes: Tigrayan forces advanced south from Mekelle-aligned positions to capture Alamata and Korem after federal withdrawal.

label: Drone Strike on Enticho/Gendebta Trucks
notes: Tigrayan officials attributed the strike to the ENDF; not independently confirmed.

label: Drone Strike on North Shewa Household
notes: Part of a documented pattern of ENDF aerial strikes on Fano-linked areas of Amhara.

label: Drone Strike on East Gojjam
notes: One of the deadliest single strikes documented in the March 2026 Amhara reporting window.

label: OLA Claimed Offensive Toward Central Oromia
notes: OLA claim of a major operation within ~100km of Addis Ababa; government did not confirm figures.

label: Fano Contests B22/B31 Roads to Bahir Dar
notes: Fano offensives since March 2026 threatened the two main approach roads into the Amhara regional capital.

label: ENDF Counteroffensive Into South Gondar
notes: Roughly 20,000 ENDF troops reported deployed to reassert control over South Gondar zone ahead of the June election.

label: Coordinated Attacks on Teleta Gebriel
notes: Attacks beginning May 30 continued through the June 1 election; OLA denies deliberately targeting civilians.

label: Shererina Battle: ENDF-TPLF Engagement
notes: Clashes involving drones, heavy artillery, and mechanized units began ~6am and lasted roughly 11 hours; TPLF's 'Army 70' unit reportedly involved.

label: TPLF 'Army 70' Staging From Sudan Side
notes: TPLF unit reportedly based across the border in Sudan moved to engage ENDF forces at Shererina; unverified.

label: Refugee Flow: Shererina to Hamdayet, Sudan
notes: Hundreds of Tigrayans, including wounded fighters, crossed into Sudan via Hamdayet following the Shererina clashes.

label: Civilian Displacement: Humera Corridor
notes: Compounding an already dire humanitarian situation, civilians near Humera fled toward the Sudanese border alongside fighters.

label: Drone Strike on Merewa Secondary School
notes: Tigrayan military sources and the district governor gave conflicting casualty breakdowns for the same strike.

label: Repeated Follow-On Strikes in Raya Alamata
notes: Multiple additional drone strikes reported in the Raya Alamata district the same morning as the school strike.

label: Ethiopia's Push for Assab Access
notes: Ethiopian officials have repeatedly signaled intent to regain sea access via Assab, prompting Eritrean accusations of war preparation.

label: Egypt-Eritrea Maritime Corridor: Assab-Massawa
notes: A May 2026 Egypt-Eritrea maritime pact revived commercial and strategic use of both Red Sea ports.

label: Afar Region Accuses TPLF-Linked Cross-Border Activity
notes: Afar regional government accused TPLF elements of crossing borders and attacking civilians in late 2025/early 2026; TPLF denied and blamed 'Ethiopian-backed militants.'

label: Alleged 'Tsimdo' Coordination Line: Port Sudan-Asmara
notes: Unverified alleged coordination between Eritrean, TPLF, and other opposition actors around the May 2026 Port Sudan gathering.

label: Drone Strike on Mekelle's Hawelti Sub-City
casualties: Part of 13 wounded across two strikes (5 children, 7 women)
notes: Struck a residential neighborhood in Hawelti Sub-City (Momona Kebele) near St. Mary Church; TPLF attributes the strike to the federal government, which has not confirmed or denied responsibility. Precise strike time is approximate based on 'early hours' reporting.

label: Second Drone Strike Near Mekelle University
notes: TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa reported a second strike near Mekelle University the same morning as the Hawelti strike; casualty breakdown between the two sites not separately confirmed.

label: Election-Day Security Closures: Amhara-Oromia
notes: At least 143 polling stations closed across Amhara and Oromia on election day due to security incidents, alongside 8 fully cancelled Amhara constituencies.
